swayable.summary: A candidate explains his detailed plan to regulate data centers by requiring them to lower electric bills, reduce property taxes, protect farmland, and meet environmental standards. He speaks directly to a voter's question in a Q&A setting, listing his conditions firmly and without hedging.
swayable.title: My Data Center Plan: Lower Bills, Clean Water, Farmland Off Limits

traits.change: Add a line like: 'As a veteran who served this state, I know what it means to protect what we've built here.'

traits.quote: not paid for by the taxpayer, but by the excess reserve that the data center has to bring in behind the meter
traits.change: This contrast is already clear; if you want to drop it, remove 'not paid for by the taxpayer, but by the excess reserve' and just say 'paid for by the data center.'
The script reads like a live Q&A with a throat-clear and applause, suggesting raw footage; reshoot with a clean backdrop, professional audio, and edited cuts to raise production quality.

traits.quote: That's common sense. We have a lot of those.
traits.change: This plain-spoken moment is already present; to drop it, replace 'That's common sense. We have a lot of those.' with a more formal policy statement like 'This is consistent with sound land-use policy.'

traits.quote: my job as a governor is to set this straight with statewide legislation
traits.change: This clearly marks the speaker as a politician running for governor; to drop it, remove 'my job as a governor' and say 'the right move is statewide legislation' instead.
Add a line like: 'I grew up near a factory that drained our town's water, and I'm not letting that happen again on my watch.'
Add a closing line like: 'If you want these protections in place, vote for me on Election Day.'

traits.quote: Thank you very much and I appreciate that question. Thank you.
traits.change: Enthusiasm shows in the warm close and the applause moment; to drop it, end with a flat statement like 'That concludes my answer on data centers.' and cut the applause.

traits.quote: I don't think you should cause a community to pay higher electric bills. I think you should cause the community to pay lower electric bills by putting more energy into the grid than you're taking out.
traits.change: This explanation of how the grid works is already present; to drop it, cut the sentence starting 'I think you should cause the community' and just say 'data centers must contribute to the grid.'
Add a line like: 'I've heard from families in this state who saw their electric bills double after a data center moved in nearby.'

traits.quote: we're blessed with in this state
traits.change: This expression of pride in the state's farmland is already present; to drop it, replace 'which we're blessed with in this state' with 'which exists across this state.'

traits.quote: you're going to get free residential electricity, not paid for by the taxpayer, but by the excess reserve that the data center has to bring in behind the meter
traits.change: The idea of free residential electricity funded by data center reserves is likely new to most viewers; to drop it, replace this with a general statement like 'residents will see lower electric costs.'
Add a light line like: 'I guess the data centers figured nobody was paying attention — well, we were paying attention, right on our electric bills.'
Add a celebrity endorser intro like: '[Name], a well-known figure from this state, introduces the candidate before the Q&A begins.'

traits.quote: They've done a horrible job of earning public trust
traits.change: This is the clearest moment of anger toward data centers; to drop it, replace 'They've done a horrible job of earning public trust' with 'public trust in data centers has not been well established.'

The speech sounds natural and unscripted, with a throat-clear and conversational phrasing; to make it sound more scripted, remove the throat-clear and rewrite the answer as a clean numbered list delivered to camera.
Add a line like: 'I've heard from farmers and families across this state who told me this is exactly the kind of protection they've been waiting for.'

traits.quote: Lower to no electric bills, lower property taxes, clean air, clean water, industrial sites only, not fertile farmland, and process transparency.
traits.change: This clear policy summary is already present; to drop it, remove this list and end with a general statement like 'my plan will protect residents and the environment.'

traits.quote: Lower property taxes, lower electric bills
traits.change: The positive vision of lower bills and taxes is already present; to drop it, remove the benefits framing and focus only on what data centers must not do.

traits.quote: They've done a horrible job of earning public trust
traits.change: This negative tone toward data centers is already present; to drop it, replace 'They've done a horrible job of earning public trust' with 'public trust still needs to be built.'
The throat-clear and live Q&A format suggest unpolished footage; to drop the amateur feel, edit out the throat-clear and reshoot the answer in a controlled setting with steady framing.
Add a line like: 'According to the state utility commission's latest report, residential rates have risen 18 percent in counties with new data centers.'

Add on-screen text displaying the five policy points as the candidate lists them: 'Lower/No Electric Bills,' 'Lower Property Taxes,' 'Clean Air & Water,' 'Industrial Sites Only,' 'Process Transparency.'

traits.quote: Are you going to try to work something out with the data centers
traits.change: The everyday voter asking the opening question is already present; to drop this, remove the voter's question and start directly with the candidate's answer to camera.

traits.quote: I don't think that you should get a property tax abatement.
traits.change: Opinion advocacy is central to this script; to drop it, replace 'I don't think' statements with neutral descriptions like 'the policy would require data centers to pay full property taxes.'
Add a line like: 'There are communities in this state that have already lost clean water and cheap power, and that loss is real and it is serious.'
Add a line like: 'If we don't act now, every family in this state could be looking at electric bills they simply cannot afford.'
Add a short animated graphic showing a data center connected to a grid with arrows flowing back into homes to illustrate the 'excess reserve behind the meter' concept.
